newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-ASC examines McIntosh share trades.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-ASC examines McIntosh share trades.

text.p: The Australian Securities Commission (ASC) said it was examining share transactions in McIntosh Securities Ltd prior to the A$1.40 per share friendly takeover offer by Merrill Lynch and Co Inc.
"We are having a look at it. Anything that has a large price rise like that will be looked at," ASC spokeswoman Irene O'Brien told Reuters.
"We are simply having a routine look at a large share price increase. It is not anywhere near an investigation and probably won't be," she said.
O'Brien said the ASC had spoken informally with the Australian Stock Exchange (ASX) about the transactions.
She said the ASC noted that much of McIntosh's share price rise began late last week when rumours of a bid by the giant United States brokerage firm were around the share market.
McIntosh shares, which last traded on Wednesday at A$1.35, first drew attention last Thursday when they gained four cents to close at A$1.10.
The stock jumped to A$1.25 the following day when the takeover rumour had been widely reported in the media.
By contrast, the stock traded in a narrow 90 to 92 cent range in the previous week, with a year's high of A$1.00 and a low of 60 cents.
The 52-week low was struck mid-year when the brokerage firm revealed it faced an exposure of up to A$17 million from its role as underwriter in the float of the Grand Hotel group.

ING Bank of the Netherlands, the largest shareholder in McIntosh with a 20 percent stake, took up a significant portion of the Grand Hotel shares, with speculation then emerging that ING was a likely seller of McIntosh, which it gained following its purchase of Barings.
ING has not yet said if it will accept the Merrill bid, which values McIntosh at A$117 million.
The ASC said last month it was conducting a high-level inquiry into questionable share dealings in transport firm TNT Ltd.
In this case, the regulator's examination focussed on options purchases just before the transport firm received a friendly and generous takeover bid from Koninklijke PTT Nederland NV.
